summary:
As global temperatures rise, urban centers face severe heat island effects, leaving densely populated neighborhoods dangerously exposed to extreme heat and poor air quality. EcoPulse is an innovative web application that bridges this gap by transforming complex, high-altitude NASA Earth observation data into actionable, hyper-local insights.

By leveraging data from sources like NASA ECOSTRESS and MODIS, EcoPulse delivers a real-time climate stress dashboard for everyday citizens and city planners alike. Key features include an interactive Neighborhood Heat Map to check local environmental conditions, a "Cool-Path" routing system that calculates the shadiest and coolest walking routes, and an urban planning sandbox to simulate the localized temperature-reduction benefits of green roofs and reflective pavements. EcoPulse empowers communities with the precise data they need to navigate urban climate stress and build cooler, more resilient cities.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

EcoPulse is an interactive geospatial web application that translates high-altitude NASA Earth observation data into hyper-local, street-level climate insights to combat the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect.

  • Telemetry & Heat Mapping: Users can inspect specific neighborhoods across metro areas (such as Kollam, New York, Tokyo, and London) to view real-time Land Surface Temperature (LST), Air Quality Index (AQI), and tree canopy shade coverage.
  • "Cool-Path" Commuter Routing: Instead of optimizing purely for the shortest distance, EcoPulse calculates pedestrian and cycling routes that maximize tree canopy and building shadow cover, comparing heat exposure against standard routes and issuing proactive hydration and heat-health advisories.
  • Urban Planning Simulator: A sandbox mode allows users and municipal planners to adjust sliders for green roof coverage, urban tree planting, and reflective cool pavements, dynamically recalculating projected afternoon cooling curves and updating thermal zone overlays on the map.

Key Benefits

  • Actionable Daily Protection: Gives everyday commuters, outdoor workers, and vulnerable residents an immediate way to reduce heat stress during daily travel.
  • Data-Driven Urban Planning: Lets local authorities and community organizations test the cooling return on investment (ROI) of green infrastructure before committing physical budgets.
  • Accessibility: Presents complex satellite raster telemetry in an intuitive, color-coded visual dashboard that requires zero scientific background to interpret.

Intended Impact

EcoPulse bridges the gap between orbital Earth science and street-level public health. By identifying thermal hotspots and pairing them with both immediate personal mitigation (Cool-Path routing) and long-term structural solutions (the Planning Simulator), the project aims to lower heat-related health risks, guide equitable tree-planting and cool-pavement initiatives in high-stress neighborhoods, and build climate-resilient cities.

Tools, Languages, Software & Data Sources

  • NASA Open Data & APIs: Designed around NASA ECOSTRESS and MODIS (Terra/Aqua) for Land Surface Temperature and vegetation indices, NASA POWER API for meteorological and solar irradiance baselines, and NASA SEDAC for urban vulnerability context.
  • Frontend Languages & Frameworks: HTML5, CSS3 (Tailwind CSS), and JavaScript (ES6+) for a fast, responsive, zero-install browser interface.
  • Mapping & Visualization Libraries: Leaflet.js paired with Esri World Dark Gray Canvas tiles (plus a custom offline canvas radar grid fallback) for geospatial rendering, and Chart.js for real-time diurnal temperature modeling.
  • Backend / Data Pipeline Architecture: Python (FastAPI/Flask, Pandas, NumPy, Rasterio) for ingesting and parsing satellite GeoTIFF/JSON datasets into lightweight frontend telemetry.
  • Development & Deployment Software: Visual Studio Code with Live Server for local prototyping, and static web hosting (GitHub Pages / Netlify) for cross-device judge access.

What Makes the Project Creative

  • Dual-Scale Solution: Most climate apps focus exclusively on either passive weather alerts or macro-level policy charts. EcoPulse connects both ends of the spectrum—helping a pedestrian cross a hot city block safely today while helping a city planner cool that exact block next year.
  • Interactive "What-If" Simulation: Turning scientific urban albedo and evapotranspiration models into tactile sliders with live map feedback makes climate science engaging and exploratory.
  • Resilient Engineering: Built with a self-healing map architecture featuring automatic offline grid fallbacks and keyless tile layers so field demonstrations work reliably even under restricted network conditions.

Key Factors Considered

  • Vulnerable Populations & Equity: Prioritized heat-stress scoring in dense urban corridors with low canopy cover, where residents are disproportionately exposed to extreme heat.
  • Latency & Usability: Designed the interface to load fast on both desktop workstations and mobile devices without heavy 3D rendering bottlenecks, ensuring practical usability outdoors in bright conditions.
  • Scientific Grounding vs. Simplicity: Balanced realistic thermodynamic cooling estimates (from tree shade, evapotranspiration, and surface albedo) with clean, plain-language metrics (°C/°F, shade percentage, and heat-risk tiers).
